summary: Defines the runtime-checkable Backend Protocol: name, connect/close and context-manager lifecycle, list_tables/list_namespaces/list_catalogs, inspect_table/inspect_namespace/inspect_catalog, raw_driver_connection(), supports_transactions, transaction(required=...), native_transaction_open() and in_transaction(). Implementations satisfy it structurally, without inheritance.
extension_points: Any class that implements every Backend member satisfies isinstance(obj, Backend); tests/test_unit/core/test_protocol.py uses a non-Ibis _StubBackend to keep the protocol backend-agnostic.
lifecycle_notes: connect() and close() return self, so construction, connection and use can be chained or used as a context manager.
transaction() is a reentrant, flat unit of work: the outermost scope owns COMMIT/ROLLBACK unless it joins a caller-opened native transaction; nested scopes join and there are no savepoints.
in_transaction() is total: it returns False and never raises for unsupported, unconnected or closed backends.
raw_driver_connection() raises rather than returning None when no driver handle is available.
documentation_hooks: Contract chapter: list every member and its guarantees.
Transaction ownership semantics: owner vs. joiner, poisoned units, required=False no-op with a one-time warning.
Difference between in_transaction() (package scope registered) and native_transaction_open() (driver state).
risks: Every member added to a runtime_checkable Protocol is a breaking change for third-party implementations; the transaction members and raw_driver_connection were added after the original lifecycle and inspection contract.
